summary: Yaroslav Vassilkov is an Indologist who studied at the Faculty of Oriental Studies of St. Petersburg University (~1961–1967). He held posts at the Imperial Academy of Sciences (~1978) and the Faculty of Philosophy at Saint Petersburg State University.

Yasuaki Nara specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1973) under Hajime Nakamura and Kogen Mizuno, and at the University of Calcutta (~1956–1959). He held posts at Komazawa University and the Soto Zen Research Center.

Yasuhiko Nagano is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, the University of Tokyo, and UC Berkeley (Ph.D. ~1976–1983). His posts include the National Museum of Ethnology, Berkeley, NIHU, and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.
Yasuhiko Sueki is a scholar of philosophy and Sinology who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held a post as professor emeritus at Komazawa University (~2018).

Yasuhiro Okazaki works in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Hiroshima University, studying under Atsushi Uno, Shoryu Katsura, and Hiroakira Ono. His career includes posts at Hiroshima Prefectural Chiyoda, Kabe Senior, and Takamiya High Schools (attested 2005).

Yasuhiro Sueki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied briefly under George Baumann at Tübingen University Library (~1988–1989). He held positions at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1980–1996) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996, ~2008).
Yasuhiro Ueno is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2003–2004). He held a post as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University (attested 2004).

Yasuhiro Yamazaki specialized in Buddhist studies and studied at Koyasan University (~1950–1954). He served as an associate professor at Shuchiin University (1966–2000) and as a professor at Koyasan University (~1975–2000).

Yasuke Ikari is an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University (~1960–1968) under Masaaki Hattori and earned a PhD from the University of Chicago (~1968–1973). He held posts at Kyoto University, Kindai University, the National Museum of Ethnology, and Harvard University.

Yasumasa Sekine specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1969–1975) and SOAS (~1982–1984). He held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology, Gakushuin Women's Junior College, University of Tsukuba, Japan Women's University, and Kwansei Gakuin University.

Yasuo Deguchi works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having completed his doctoral studies at Kyoto University (~1991–1996). He held academic posts at Nagoya Institute of Technology, Kyoto University (2002–2025), and ZEN University (2025), and founded the Kyoto Institute of Philosophy.
Yasuo Goto is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held lecturing posts at Ryukoku University (attested 1991, 2006) and Shuchiin University (attested 2006).
Yasuo Inamoto specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a technical official at Nara National Museum (~1994–2002) and at Kyoto University (~2004).

Yasuo Matsunami specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, completing doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also studied under Ryukai Mano. He served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 1995–2006) and as an advisor to Sravakabhumi Kenkyukai (-2010).
Yasuo Sano is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996). He founded the Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.

Yasuo Yuasa specialized in philosophy and religious studies, studying at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo, University of Yamanashi, Osaka University, University of Tsukuba, and J. F. Oberlin University.

Yasuro Abe works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Wako University and Otani University. He held positions at Osaka University, Otemae University, Nagoya University, the International Research Center for Japanese Studies, and Ryukoku University.
Yasusaburo Sakaki studied at the University of Tokyo (~1891–1897). He later held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1899–1906) and Kyushu University (~1906–1925).

Yasutaka Muroya is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He has held research associate positions at the University of Vienna (attested 2007), Leipzig University (attested 2015), and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2022).

Yasutoshi Murakami works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Tohoku University (~1960–1969) and held posts at Yamaguchi University (~1974–2007), Koyasan University (~2007–2013), and the Society of Esoteric Buddhism (attested 2004).
